newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: CRICKET-AHMAD AND AKRAM BOOST PAKISTAN'S TOTAL.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-AHMAD AND AKRAM BOOST PAKISTAN'S TOTAL.

text.p: A late assault by Ijaz Ahmad and captainWasim Akram helped Pakistan to reach a respectable 234 in the final one-day international against New Zealand on Sunday.
The two batsmen shared an unbroken 108-run fifth-wicket partnership from 75 balls to lift Pakistan from a precarious 126 for four in 37.3 overs to a competitive total.

Ahmad scored an unbeaten 73 from 87 balls with the aid of six fours, while Akram cut the accurate New Zealand attack down to size by blasting five massive sixes and four blistering boundaries in his unconquered 66 off 39 balls.

Akram took 21 runs from Justin Vaughan's final over, punishing him with two sixes and two fours. Vaughan, who had conceded only 14 runs in a fine six-over opening spell, finished the day with one wicket for 59 runs from his 10-over quota.

Opener Zahoor Elahi also batted with confidence and authority, scoring 51 from 99 balls with six boundaries and a six over point off Chris Cairns. He was bowled round his legs while trying to sweep Matthew Hart.

Hart had Inzamamul Haq stumped for seven in his first over. The burly middle-order batsman, who had scored 14 and 2 in his last two innings, struggled for 28 balls before the left-arm spinner tempted him down the track and beat him with the flight.
